instruction: Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, module `VSAOps`, giving the core Vector Symbolic Architecture operations over balanced-ternary hypervectors. Open with the Apache-2.0 SPDX line and the project's `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` banner, then `use base::types` and `use base::ops`. Define VSA_DIM = 1024, SIMD_WIDTH = 32, MAX_VECTORS = 32, the metric selectors SIM_COSINE/SIM_HAMMING/SIM_DOT, and BIND_IDENTITY/BIND_INVERT. Implement over `[]Trit` with an explicit `len` parameter: `bind` (zero acts as identity, two non-zero trits multiply), `unbind` (the same operation, since bind is self-inverse), `bundle2` and `bundle3` as sign-of-sum majority votes, `similarity` dispatching on the metric constant, `cosine_similarity`, `hamming_similarity`, `dot_product`, `vector_norm` (sqrt of the non-zero trit count) and `hamming_distance`. Add `permute` as a circular shift, plus `encode_sequence` and `probe_sequence` built on it. Then add a fixed 27-trit layer for Coptic-letter encoding: `coptic_bind`, `coptic_unbind`, `coptic_bundle3` and `coptic_similarity` over `[27]Trit`. Tests use the `given`/`and`/`when`/`then` form and must pin the exact trit results of bind, bundle2/3, dot product, norm, cosine similarity and permute, including the bind/unbind round trip. Invariants must state the algebra: bind commutative, associative and self-inverse, zero vector is the bind identity, bundle2/bundle3 commutative, permute undone by the complementary shift, cosine bounded to [-1,1] and Hamming to [0,1], self-similarity 1.0, and bind distributing over bundle2. Close with `bench` blocks using `measure:`/`target:` lines for each operation at dimension 1024.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, module `zig_runtime`, that is the Zig backend code generator for the `tri` CLI runtime. Pull in the runtime specs with the `using name: @import("...")` form for `compiler/runtime/commands.t27` and `compiler/runtime/validation.t27`. Export three generator functions returning `[]const u8` built by `++` string concatenation: `generate_main()` emits a main.zig whose `pub fn main() !u8` allocates process args, falls back to `commands.help("")` when there are fewer than two, and delegates to a `dispatch_command` that matches on spec, gen, git, lint, skill and help and returns 1 for anything unknown; `generate_commands_module()` emits commands.zig with `spec_dispatch` (create/validate/list), `gen_dispatch`, `git_dispatch` (status/commit/push), `lint_dispatch` and `skill_dispatch` (begin/seal/status), plus `parse_bool_flag` and `parse_string_flag` helpers; `generate_validation_module()` emits validation.zig with a `ValidationResult` struct and `validate_tdd_contract`, `validate_language_policy` (reject Cyrillic outside docs/) and `validate_generated_header`. Every emitted file must begin with a header naming its source .t27, a DO NOT EDIT warning and a generation timestamp. Add thin `generate_*_zig()` wrappers and a `generate_runtime_zig()` that writes all three under `src/tri/` and returns 0. Put the tests, invariants and benches after the module body: tests assert the generated text contains the expected headers, the dispatch function and the imports; invariants assert every generated file carries the DO NOT EDIT warning and that all five dispatch functions are present; benches give a `target:` latency for each generator.
output:
// runtime.t27 -- Zig Runtime Code Generation
// Generates Zig backend from compiler/runtime/*.t27 specifications
// phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY

module zig_runtime {
    using commands: @import("compiler/runtime/commands.t27");
    using validation: @import("compiler/runtime/validation.t27");

    // =====================================================================
    // Zig Runtime Generation
    // =====================================================================

    // Generate main.zig entry point
    pub fn generate_main() []const u8 {
        return "// This file is generated from compiler/runtime/runtime.t27\n" ++
               "// DO NOT EDIT - Changes will be overwritten on next tri gen\n" ++
               "// Generated at: " ++ get_current_timestamp() ++ "\n" ++
               "// Source spec: compiler/runtime/runtime.t27\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "const std = @import(\"std\");\n" ++
               "const commands = @import(\"commands.zig\");\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "pub fn main() !u8 {\n" ++
               "    const allocator = std.heap.page_allocator;\n" ++
               "    const args = try std.process.argsAlloc(allocator);\n" ++
               "    defer std.process.argsFree(allocator, args);\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    if (args.len < 2) {\n" ++
               "        try commands.help(\"\");\n" ++
               "        return 0;\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    const command = args[1];\n" ++
               "    const command_args = args[2..];\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    return dispatch_command(command, command_args);\n" ++
               "}\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "fn dispatch_command(command: []const u8, args: [][]const u8) !u8 {\n" ++
               "    if (std.mem.eql(u8, command, \"spec\")) {\n" ++
               "        return commands.spec_dispatch(args);\n" ++
               "    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, command, \"gen\")) {\n" ++
               "        return commands.gen_dispatch(args);\n" ++
               "    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, command, \"git\")) {\n" ++
               "        return commands.git_dispatch(args);\n" ++
               "    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, command, \"lint\")) {\n" ++
               "        return commands.lint_dispatch(args);\n" ++
               "    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, command, \"skill\")) {\n" ++
               "        return commands.skill_dispatch(args);\n" ++
               "    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, command, \"help\")) {\n" ++
               "        try commands.help(if (args.len > 0) args[0] else \"\");\n" ++
               "        return 0;\n" ++
               "    } else {\n" ++
               "        std.debug.print(\"Unknown command: {s}\\n\", .{command});\n" ++
               "        try commands.help(\"\");\n" ++
               "        return 1;\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "}\n";
    }

    // Generate commands.zig
    pub fn generate_commands_module() []const u8 {
        return "// This file is generated from compiler/runtime/commands.t27\n" ++
               "// DO NOT EDIT - Changes will be overwritten on next tri gen\n" ++
               "// Generated at: " ++ get_current_timestamp() ++ "\n" ++
               "// Source spec: compiler/runtime/commands.t27\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "const std = @import(\"std\");\n" ++
               "const validation = @import(\"validation.zig\");\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "pub fn spec_dispatch(args: [][]const u8) !u8 {\n" ++
               "    if (args.len < 1) {\n" ++
               "        try help(\"spec\");\n" ++
               "        return 0;\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    const subcommand = args[0];\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    if (std.mem.eql(u8, subcommand, \"create\")) {\n" ++
               "        if (args.len < 2) {\n" ++
               "            std.debug.print(\"ERROR: spec name required\\n\", .{});\n" ++
               "            return 1;\n" ++
               "        }\n" ++
               "        const name = args[1];\n" ++
               "        const kind = if (args.len > 2) args[2] else \"feature\";\n" ++
               "        return spec_create(name, kind);\n" ++
               "    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, subcommand, \"validate\")) {\n" ++
               "        if (args.len < 2) {\n" ++
               "            std.debug.print(\"ERROR: spec path required\\n\", .{});\n" ++
               "            return 1;\n" ++
               "        }\n" ++
               "        return spec_validate(args[1]);\n" ++
               "    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, subcommand, \"list\")) {\n" ++
               "        return spec_list();\n" ++
               "    } else {\n" ++
               "        try help(\"spec\");\n" ++
               "        return 1;\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "}\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "pub fn gen_dispatch(args: [][]const u8) !u8 {\n" ++
               "    if (args.len == 0 or std.mem.eql(u8, args[0], \"--all\")) {\n" ++
               "        const backend = if (args.len > 1) args[1] else \"zig\";\n" ++
               "        return gen_all(backend);\n" ++
               "    } else {\n" ++
               "        const spec_path = args[0];\n" ++
               "        const backend = if (args.len > 1) args[1] else \"zig\";\n" ++
               "        return gen_spec(spec_path, backend, false);\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "}\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "pub fn git_dispatch(args: [][]const u8) !u8 {\n" ++
               "    const allocator = std.heap.page_allocator;\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    if (args.len == 0 or std.mem.eql(u8, args[0], \"status\")) {\n" ++
               "        return git_status_with_skill();\n" ++
               "    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, args[0], \"commit\")) {\n" ++
               "        const all = parse_bool_flag(args, \"--all\");\n" ++
               "        const message = parse_string_flag(args, \"-m\");\n" ++
               "        const mode = parse_string_flag(args, \"--mode\") orelse \"normal\";\n" ++
               "        return git_commit(all, message, mode);\n" ++
               "    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, args[0], \"push\")) {\n" ++
               "        const mode = parse_string_flag(args, \"--mode\") orelse \"normal\";\n" ++
               "        return git_push(\"\", \"\", mode);\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    return 0;\n" ++
               "}\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "pub fn lint_dispatch(args: [][]const u8) !u8 {\n" ++
               "    const strict = parse_bool_flag(args, \"--strict\");\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    if (args.len == 0 or std.mem.eql(u8, args[0], \"--all\")) {\n" ++
               "        return lint_all(strict);\n" ++
               "    } else {\n" ++
               "        return lint_file(args[0], strict);\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "}\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "pub fn skill_dispatch(args: [][]const u8) !u8 {\n" ++
               "    if (args.len == 0) {\n" ++
               "        return skill_status();\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    const subcommand = args[0];\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    if (std.mem.eql(u8, subcommand, \"begin\")) {\n" ++
               "        const issue = parse_string_flag(args, \"--issue\") orelse \"\";\n" ++
               "        const kind = parse_string_flag(args, \"--kind\") orelse \"feature\";\n" ++
               "        return skill_begin(issue, kind);\n" ++
               "    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, subcommand, \"seal\")) {\n" ++
               "        return skill_seal();\n" ++
               "    } else if (std.mem.eql(u8, subcommand, \"status\")) {\n" ++
               "        return skill_status();\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    return 0;\n" ++
               "}\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "fn parse_bool_flag(args: [][]const u8, flag: []const u8) bool {\n" ++
               "    for (args) |arg| {\n" ++
               "        if (std.mem.eql(u8, arg, flag)) return true;\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "    return false;\n" ++
               "}\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "fn parse_string_flag(args: [][]const u8, flag: []const u8) ?[]const u8 {\n" ++
               "    var i: usize = 0;\n" ++
               "    while (i < args.len - 1) : (i += 1) {\n" ++
               "        if (std.mem.eql(u8, args[i], flag)) {\n" ++
               "            return args[i + 1];\n" ++
               "        }\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "    return null;\n" ++
               "}\n";
    }

    // Generate validation.zig
    pub fn generate_validation_module() []const u8 {
        return "// This file is generated from compiler/runtime/validation.t27\n" ++
               "// DO NOT EDIT - Changes will be overwritten on next tri gen\n" ++
               "// Generated at: " ++ get_current_timestamp() ++ "\n" ++
               "// Source spec: compiler/runtime/validation.t27\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "const std = @import(\"std\");\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "pub const ValidationResult = struct {\n" ++
               "    valid: bool,\n" ++
               "    error_msg: []const u8,\n" ++
               "    hint: []const u8,\n" ++
               "};\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "pub fn validate_tdd_contract(spec_path: []const u8) !ValidationResult {\n" ++
               "    const content = try std.fs.cwd().readFileAlloc(\n" ++
               "        std.heap.page_allocator,\n" ++
               "        spec_path,\n" ++
               "        1024 * 1024,\n" ++
               "    );\n" ++
               "    defer std.heap.page_allocator.free(content);\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    const has_test = std.mem.indexOf(u8, content, \".test\") != null;\n" ++
               "    const has_invariant = std.mem.indexOf(u8, content, \".invariant\") != null;\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    if (!has_test and !has_invariant) {\n" ++
               "        return ValidationResult{\n" ++
               "            .valid = false,\n" ++
               "            .error_msg = \"TDD contract violated: spec must contain at least one 'test' or 'invariant' block\",\n" ++
               "            .hint = \"See: docs/TDD-CONTRACT.md\",\n" ++
               "        };\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    return ValidationResult{\n" ++
               "        .valid = true,\n" ++
               "        .error_msg = \"\",\n" ++
               "        .hint = \"\",\n" ++
               "    };\n" ++
               "}\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "pub fn validate_language_policy(spec_path: []const u8) !ValidationResult {\n" ++
               "    if (std.mem.startsWith(u8, spec_path, \"docs/\")) {\n" ++
               "        return ValidationResult{ .valid = true, .error_msg = \"\", .hint = \"\" };\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    const content = try std.fs.cwd().readFileAlloc(\n" ++
               "        std.heap.page_allocator,\n" ++
               "        spec_path,\n" ++
               "        1024 * 1024,\n" ++
               "    );\n" ++
               "    defer std.heap.page_allocator.free(content);\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    for (content) |c| {\n" ++
               "        if (c >= 0x0400 and c <= 0x04FF) {\n" ++
               "            return ValidationResult{\n" ++
               "                .valid = false,\n" ++
               "                .error_msg = \"Language policy violated: source file contains Cyrillic characters\",\n" ++
               "                .hint = \"Source files must be ASCII-only. See: ADR-004-language-policy.md\",\n" ++
               "            };\n" ++
               "        }\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    return ValidationResult{\n" ++
               "        .valid = true,\n" ++
               "        .error_msg = \"\",\n" ++
               "        .hint = \"\",\n" ++
               "    };\n" ++
               "}\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "pub fn validate_generated_header(zig_path: []const u8) !ValidationResult {\n" ++
               "    const file = try std.fs.cwd().openFile(zig_path, .{});\n" ++
               "    defer file.close();\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    const reader = file.reader();\n" ++
               "    var line_buffer: [256]u8 = undefined;\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    const line1 = try reader.readUntilDelimiterOrEof(&line_buffer, '\\n') orelse \"\";\n" ++
               "    if (!std.mem.indexOf(u8, line1, \"This file is generated from\") != null) {\n" ++
               "        return ValidationResult{\n" ++
               "            .valid = false,\n" ++
               "            .error_msg = \"Zig file lacks generated header\",\n" ++
               "            .hint = \"Write .t27 spec first, then run 'tri gen'\",\n" ++
               "        };\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    const line2 = try reader.readUntilDelimiterOrEof(&line_buffer, '\\n') orelse \"\";\n" ++
               "    if (!std.mem.indexOf(u8, line2, \"DO NOT EDIT\") != null) {\n" ++
               "        return ValidationResult{\n" ++
               "            .valid = false,\n" ++
               "            .error_msg = \"Zig file header missing 'DO NOT EDIT' warning\",\n" ++
               "            .hint = \"Generated files must not be edited\",\n" ++
               "        };\n" ++
               "    }\n" ++
               "\n" ++
               "    return ValidationResult{\n" ++
               "        .valid = true,\n" ++
               "        .error_msg = \"\",\n" ++
               "        .hint = \"\",\n" ++
               "    };\n" ++
               "}\n";
    }

    // Generate src/tri/main.zig (entry point)
    pub fn generate_main_zig() []const u8 {
        return generate_main();
    }

    // Generate src/tri/commands.zig
    pub fn generate_commands_zig() []const u8 {
        return generate_commands_module();
    }

    // Generate src/tri/validation.zig
    pub fn generate_validation_zig() []const u8 {
        return generate_validation_module();
    }

    // =====================================================================
    // Code generation entry point
    // =====================================================================

    // Generate all Zig runtime files
    pub fn generate_runtime_zig() i32 {
        const base_dir = "src/tri/";
        create_dir_if_not_exists(base_dir);

        write_file(base_dir ++ "main.zig", generate_main_zig());
        write_file(base_dir ++ "commands.zig", generate_commands_zig());
        write_file(base_dir ++ "validation.zig", generate_validation_zig());

        print("Generated Zig runtime:");
        print("  " ++ base_dir ++ "main.zig");
        print("  " ++ base_dir ++ "commands.zig");
        print("  " ++ base_dir ++ "validation.zig");

        return 0;
    }
}

// =======================================================================================================
// TDD-Inside-Spec: Tests and Invariants for Runtime Code Generation
// =======================================================================================================

test generate_main_contains_header
    const main_zig = zig_runtime.generate_main();
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, main_zig, "This file is generated from compiler/runtime/runtime.t27") != null);

test generate_main_contains_dispatch_function
    const main_zig = zig_runtime.generate_main();
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, main_zig, "fn dispatch_command") != null);

test generate_main_includes_commands_import
    const main_zig = zig_runtime.generate_main();
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, main_zig, "const commands = @import") != null);

test generate_commands_module_contains_spec_dispatch
    const commands_zig = zig_runtime.generate_commands_module();
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, commands_zig, "pub fn spec_dispatch") != null);

test generate_commands_module_contains_validation_import
    const commands_zig = zig_runtime.generate_commands_module();
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, commands_zig, "const validation = @import") != null);

test generate_validation_module_contains_tdd_contract_check
    const validation_zig = zig_runtime.generate_validation_module();
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, validation_zig, "validate_tdd_contract") != null);

test generate_validation_module_contains_language_policy_check
    const validation_zig = zig_runtime.generate_validation_module();
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, validation_zig, "validate_language_policy") != null);

test generate_validation_module_contains_header_check
    const validation_zig = zig_runtime.generate_validation_module();
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, validation_zig, "validate_generated_header") != null);

test generate_runtime_zig_returns_zero_on_success
    const result = zig_runtime.generate_runtime_zig();
    assert(result == 0);

invariant generate_main_always_includes_header
    // generate_main always includes generated header
    const main_zig = zig_runtime.generate_main();
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, main_zig, "This file is generated from") != null);

invariant generate_main_always_has_main_function
    // generate_main always exports pub fn main()
    const main_zig = zig_runtime.generate_main();
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, main_zig, "pub fn main() !u8") != null);

invariant generate_commands_module_always_has_dispatch_functions
    // generate_commands_module generates all dispatch functions
    const commands_zig = zig_runtime.generate_commands_module();
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, commands_zig, "pub fn spec_dispatch") != null);
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, commands_zig, "pub fn gen_dispatch") != null);
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, commands_zig, "pub fn git_dispatch") != null);
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, commands_zig, "pub fn lint_dispatch") != null);
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, commands_zig, "pub fn skill_dispatch") != null);

invariant generate_validation_module_defines_validation_result
    // generate_validation_module defines ValidationResult struct
    const validation_zig = zig_runtime.generate_validation_module();
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, validation_zig, "pub const ValidationResult = struct") != null);

invariant all_generated_files_have_do_not_edit_header
    // All generated files contain "DO NOT EDIT" warning
    const main_zig = zig_runtime.generate_main();
    const commands_zig = zig_runtime.generate_commands_module();
    const validation_zig = zig_runtime.generate_validation_module();
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, main_zig, "DO NOT EDIT") != null);
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, commands_zig, "DO NOT EDIT") != null);
    assert(std.mem.indexOf(u8, validation_zig, "DO NOT EDIT") != null);

bench generate_main_latency
    target: < 10us
    const result = zig_runtime.generate_main();
    _ = result;

bench generate_commands_module_latency
    target: < 50us
    const result = zig_runtime.generate_commands_module();
    _ = result;

bench generate_validation_module_latency
    target: < 20us
    const result = zig_runtime.generate_validation_module();
    _ = result;

bench generate_runtime_zig_latency
    target: < 100us
    const result = zig_runtime.generate_runtime_zig();
    _ = result;

instruction: Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, module `config-migrate`, covering config version detection, upgrade and compatibility handling. Use the top-level form (`module config-migrate;` followed by `use std;` and declarations at file scope, no wrapping braces). Define MIGRATION_VERSION and MIN_SUPPORTED_VERSION as u16, MAX_MIGRATION_STEPS as u8, MIGRATION_TIMEOUT_SEC, a "version" key constant and a ".bak" backup suffix. Declare enums `MigrationResultType` (success/partial/failed/skipped), `MigrationAction` (add_field, remove_field, rename_field, change_type, set_default, migrate_value) and `MigrationSeverity` (info/warning/error/critical), and structs `MigrationStep`, `MigrationRule`, `MigrationResult`, `MigrationError`, `VersionInfo` and `MigrationContext` (dry_run, backup_enabled, force_migration, verbose). Provide `detect_version`, `is_version_supported`, `needs_migration`, constructors `step_create` / `step_with_description` / `result_success` / `result_failure` / `error_create` / `error_info` / `error_warning`, a `migrate` driver that returns a skipped result when no migration is needed and otherwise applies each rule via `apply_rule`, a `backup_path_create` / `backup_verify` pair, and four context constructors (default, dry run, force, verbose). Tests should cover version detection, both branches of `needs_migration`, step and result construction, the three error severities, the backup path, and each context constructor. Invariants use `@compileAssert` to pin the positive constants, the non-empty version key and backup suffix, and the enum tag values. Finish with `bench` blocks measuring version detection, the migration check, result and error creation and backup path construction.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, module `provider-adapters`, specifying the HTTP adapter layer that sits between the runtime and the AI provider APIs. Use the top-level declaration form and import `tritype-base::usize` plus `ProviderType`, `RequestParams` and `Response` from `provider-schema`. Define the timeout, retry-count and backoff defaults with a maximum backoff cap, the four HTTP method name constants, the Content-Type / Authorization / anthropic-version header strings, the status codes 200/201/401/403/404/429/500/503, and the Anthropic messages and OpenAI chat-completions endpoint URLs. Declare `HttpMethod` and `RetryPolicy` (none, exponential, linear, fixed) and `StreamAdapterState` as `enum(u8)`, and structs `HttpHeader`, `HttpRequest`, `HttpResponse`, `AdapterConfig`, `AdapterResult`, `StreamChunk`, `RateLimitInfo` and `AuthInfo`. Provide constructors for each of those, where an `HttpResponse` sets `success` from a 2xx status and `adapter_config_create` picks the endpoint from the provider type. Add predicates `is_status_success` / `client_error` / `server_error` / `rate_limited` / `unauthorized`, `is_response_success`, `is_adapter_success`, method-to-string and string-to-method, a `build_headers` that appends the anthropic-version header only for Anthropic, a `calculate_retry_delay` implementing all four policies and clamping the exponential case to the maximum, and endpoint getters. Write `test "..."` blocks in Zig style using `try std.testing.expect`, `invariant` blocks using `@compileAssert` for the enum ranges and the positive/ordered delay constants, and `bench "..."` blocks that loop each constructor 1000 times with a stated cycle target.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, module `provider-schema`, defining the message and model types shared by the AI provider adapters. Write Zig-style `test "..."` blocks that the float cycle total equals base * TRINITY within 0.001, that the decide phase equals base_ms exactly, and that the decide-to-sense duration ratio is phi squared within a 0.15 tolerance (the slack absorbs the integer truncation).

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, module `CTS_Testbench`, that is the clock-tree-synthesis testbench for `fpga::cts::CTS` — it exercises clock buffer insertion, skew balancing and latency estimation. Use the Apache-2.0 SPDX line and the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` banner. Declare a 20-unit clock period, a maximum skew of 100 ps, a maximum latency of 2000 ps, two clock domains and a 50 ps buffer delay. Declare mutable testbench state with `var`: clk, rst_n, cts_done, measured skew and latency, buffer count, and pass/fail counters. Provide a `tick()` that toggles the clock low then high, a `reset()` that holds rst_n low across two ticks and then releases it, `estimate_latency(stages, buffer_delay)` as the product, `estimate_skew(path_a_stages, path_b_stages, buffer_delay)` as the absolute stage difference times the delay computed without unsigned underflow, and `balance_tree(endpoints)` returning the number of halvings needed to reach one endpoint. Write `test` blocks with `invariant` assertion lines inside them covering: the reset state leaves cts_done false, a 4-stage latency of 200, zero skew for balanced paths, 100 ps skew for a 6-vs-4 imbalance, balance_tree of 8, 16 and 1 giving 3, 4 and 0, and the two constraint constants. Add module-level `invariant name : expr;` lines for the positive skew and buffer-delay constants, and a `bench` block that runs 100 latency and balance-tree estimates.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, module `QMTech_A100T_Integration`, giving the board-level integration profile for the QMTech XC7A100T development board. Use the Apache-2.0 SPDX line and the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` banner, and pull in `fpga::top_level::ZeroDSP_TopLevel`, `fpga::gf16_accel::Gf16Accel`, `fpga::memory::Memory` and `fpga::fifo::Fifo`. Declare the board name "qmtech-xc7a100t", part "xc7a100tcsg324-1", a 12 MHz clock, 115200 baud UART, a 0x8000-byte memory, a FIFO depth of 8, eight LEDs and the LVCMOS33 I/O standard. Define a `PinMapping` struct and a `QMTECH_PINS` constant giving clk = E3, rst = C18, uart_tx = T15, uart_rx = T14 and the eight LED pins as a comma-separated string; and a `SystemConfig` struct with a `SYS_CONFIG` constant mirroring the clock, baud, memory size and FIFO depth. Finish with module-level `invariant name : expr;` lines for a positive clock, a baud rate in (0, 921600] and a non-empty board name, plus a `bench` block calling the divisor.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, module `Simulator_Testbench`, that is the testbench for `fpga::simulator::Simulator`, exercising cycle stepping, event scheduling and waveform output. Use the Apache-2.0 SPDX line and the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` banner. Declare a 20-unit clock period, a one-million maximum cycle count and a 64-deep event queue. Declare mutable testbench state with `var`: clk, rst_n, sim_running, sim_cycle, events_processed, event_fired and the pass/fail counters. Provide a `tick()` that toggles the clock and advances the cycle counter, a `reset()` that pulses rst_n low over two ticks, releases it, ticks once more and zeroes the cycle counter, a `run_cycles(n) -> u32` that ticks n times while counting processed events and returns the current cycle, and a `schedule_event(cycle) -> bool` that refuses any cycle beyond the maximum. Write `test` blocks containing `invariant` assertion lines: after reset the simulator is not running and the cycle count is zero; 100 cycles advance both the cycle count and the event count to 100; scheduling at cycle 500 succeeds and at 2,000,000 fails; and the two capacity constants hold their values. Add a module-level `invariant max_cycles_positive : MAX_CYCLES > 0;` and a `bench` block that resets and runs 1000 cycles.

Write a very small t27 spec in the module dialect, module `chimera`, recording the best-fit gamma formula P35_new from PDG 2024 (Delta = 0.140%). Use the Apache-2.0 SPDX line, a comment naming the file and the source of the formula, and the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` banner. Inside the module, `use base::math` and `use compiler::codegen`, bind `PHI` to `base::PHI` as a `Float` constant, and export a single `pub fn formula() -> Float` returning `GAMMA.pow(PHI) + PI`, with a comment above it naming the PDG entry it encodes. Follow the module with one `test "chimera_best_gamma_smoke_test"` that just expects true — the formula has no independent reference value to check against yet, so the test exists only to satisfy the TDD contract that every spec carries at least one test block.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, module `forward_pass`, implementing a transformer-style forward pass built entirely out of Vector Symbolic Architecture operations. Use the top-level declaration form, credit the author, use the Apache-2.0 SPDX line, and import `gf16`, `Trit` and the VSA primitives bind, unbind, bundle2, bundle3, permute and cosine_similarity. Declare DEFAULT_DIM = 1024, NUM_ROLES = 11, CONTEXT_SIZE = 8, NUM_HEADS = 3, VECTORS_PER_HEAD = 3, the FF1 and FF2 role indices 9 and 10, a generation cap, a default learning rate, RESONATOR_ITERS = 5 and a similarity threshold, and define the type aliases `Hypervector`, `Roles` (laid out Q0,K0,V0 through Q2,K2,V2 then FF1, FF2) and `Context`, plus a `TrainResult` struct carrying loss, similarity and iteration count. Implement: `init_roles(dim, seed)` filling the roles deterministically; `single_head_attention` that binds the last position with the Q role, scans the context for the best-matching key by cosine similarity, and returns the winning position bound with the V role; `forward_pass_multi_head` that permutes each context slot by its index, runs three heads, merges them with bundle3, passes through the two FFN binds and adds a residual bundle2; `summarize_context` and the single-bind `forward_pass_direct`; `resonator_train_step`, which iteratively unbinds the target to get ideal FF1/FF2 directions, applies them and keeps the best loss, stopping early past the threshold; `compute_direct_role`; `generate_autoregressive`, appending each prediction and shifting the window; and the metrics `measure_perplexity` and `compute_accuracy`, both returning 0 on an empty dataset. Cover it with `test "..."` blocks, `invariant "..."` blocks asserting the role count, dimension preservation and the metric ranges, and `bench "..."` blocks.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, module `VM`, defining a ternary virtual machine for hyperdimensional computing. Use the Apache-2.0 SPDX line and the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` banner, and import rather than duplicate `base::types`, `numeric::gf16`, `vsa::vsa_core` and `ternary::hybrid_arithmetic`. Declare `VSAOpcode` as an `enum(u8)` grouping vector ops (v_load, v_store, v_const, v_random), VSA ops (v_bind, v_unbind, v_bundle2, v_bundle3), similarity ops (v_dot, v_cosine, v_hamming), arithmetic (v_add, v_neg, v_mul), control (v_mov, v_pack, v_unpack, v_cmp), permutation (v_permute, v_ipermute, v_seq) and nop/halt. Declare a `VSARegisters` struct with four HybridBigInt vector registers v0-v3, two i64 scalars, four gf16 float registers, a program counter and the cc_zero/cc_neg/cc_pos condition codes; a `VSAInstruction` struct with opcode, dst, src1, src2 and an i64 immediate; and a `VSAVM` struct holding the registers, a halted flag, a cycle count and a jit_enabled flag. Provide `vm_create()` zeroing every register, `vm_halt(vm)`, and `vm_step(vm, instruction)` which increments the cycle count and switches on the opcode, delegating bind/unbind/bundle to `vsa_core`, storing dot and hamming results into the scalar registers and cosine into f0, setting cc_zero from a zero Hamming distance on compare, and setting halted on halt. Add the `vm_get_vreg` / `vm_set_vreg` helpers, where an out-of-range index reads back a zero vector. Write tests in the `given`/`and`/`when`/`then` form covering creation, halting, each opcode's observable effect and register access; invariants that each step increments the cycle count by one, that halt is sticky and that all registers start zeroed; and `bench "..."` blocks looping each instruction 1000 times.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, module `Partition`, that partitions HIR modules across multiple FPGAs and estimates inter-FPGA bandwidth. Use the Apache-2.0 SPDX line, note in a comment that the spec uses flat arrays plus count fields for parser compatibility, and close the file with the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` banner. Define `FpgaNode` (name, device, luts, ffs, bram18, dsp48, io_pins) with a generic `fpga_node` constructor and an `arty_a7_node` preset for the xc7a100t (63400 LUTs, 126800 FFs, 135 BRAM18, 240 DSP48, 300 IO); `InterFpgaLink` with `lvds_link` (1000 Mbps per lane) and `serdes_link` (4 lanes at 6250 Mbps) constructors and a `link_bandwidth_mbps` returning width times rate; `PartitionAssign`; and `PartitionResult` with `partition_ok`, `partition_fail` and a `passed` predicate. Add `total_link_bandwidth(links, count)` summing only the first `count` entries, `fpga_util` guarding a zero-LUT node, `fpga_remaining` saturating at zero, and a `validate_node` counting every fault. Two parser constraints must be respected and called out in comments: name the assignment parameter `mod_name`, because a parameter named `module` aborts the body parse and silently drops every later declaration; and declare the link array parameter as `[]const InterFpgaLink`, because a mutable slice cannot be produced by any expression a test can write. Write tests in the `given`/`then`/`and` form covering both link types, the bandwidth sum respecting a short and a zero count, utilisation at 0, 50 and 100 percent and on a zero-LUT node, remaining capacity at exact fit and over capacity, that validation counts both faults, and that a failed partition carries its error count. Add invariants and two `bench` blocks.

Write lesson 1 of the t27 tutorial as a t27 spec in the module dialect, module `tutorial-01-values`, covering values and types. Use the Apache-2.0 SPDX line and `;`-prefixed header comments explaining that every constant carries an explicit width because a spec has to say what reaches hardware rather than let a compiler pick, and that nothing here is inferred; close the header with the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` banner. Use the top-level declaration form and declare only public constants, organised into commented sections. Show integers across widths and signedness (u8, i8, u16, u32, i32) with a section comment explaining that u/i and the number are part of the type; then hex and binary literals, with a comment arguing that binary is worth using where the value *is* a bit pattern, illustrated by a nine-bit mantissa mask; then f32, f64 and both boolean values; then the trit — TRIT_NEG, TRIT_ZERO and TRIT_POS stored in an i8, with a comment that the language is built on three states and that the invariant below is what makes the range a claim rather than a comment — plus TRINITY = 3. Finish with two `invariant name` / `assert` blocks, preceded by a comment explaining that an invariant holds for the module as a whole and is checked, not decorative: one deriving the three-state trit range from TRIT_POS - TRIT_NEG + 1, and one asserting the mantissa mask equals 511. No functions and no tests.
